definitions: Plane tangency means exactly one common point; theorem 37 makes the contact radius a normal. A sphere tangent line through a contact point is any line in that tangent plane through the contact point. All spheres here have R>0.

parts.reason: For P on a sphere centered at C, the unique plane through P normal to CP is tangent. Any tangent plane through this sphere point must have P as its sole contact and this normal.
With C=0 and |P|=d>R, a unit normal n gives a tangent plane n.X=R through P precisely when n.P=R. These normals form a nondegenerate circle, giving infinitely many distinct planes.
Every line through P in its unique tangent plane has distance R from C and exactly one contact. There is an entire pencil of such lines, not the single tangent of a planar circle.
A plane through CP cuts a great circle with two tangents through external P. Rotating this plane around CP yields a cone of distinct tangent lines; the planar count of two is not the spatial count.

parts.answer: The normal line to the given plane through O, excluding O.
parts.reason: Every center is C=O+t*n with unit plane normal n and t nonzero. The radius is |t|>0. Conversely this center and radius give exactly contact O. Both sides are allowed; t=0 is not a sphere.

parts.answer: Two parallel planes at distance R on opposite sides of the given plane.
parts.reason: For the plane n.X=b with |n|=1, centers satisfy |n.C-b|=R, hence n.C=b+R or b-R. Neither a single side nor the original plane is the full locus.

parts.answer: No unique distance follows from the unconditioned wording. If the center lies in the selected dihedral region of angle phi, d=R/sin(phi/2); if it lies in an adjacent supplementary region, d=R/cos(phi/2). Opposite selected regions have the same first distance. R>0 and 0<phi<pi.
parts.reason: Take the plane through C perpendicular to the edge. The tangent planes become intersecting lines, and the center is equally distant R from both. It lies on one of the two angle bisectors. If the containing sector angle is theta, the right triangle gives R=d*sin(theta/2). Relative to the selected sector, theta is phi or pi-phi. For phi=pi/3 the possible distances are 2R and 2R/sqrt(3); for phi=pi/2 they coincide at sqrt(2)R. Never silently choose an acute or center-containing sector.
Tangency to x=0,y=0,z=0 gives |a|=|b|=|c|=R. The explicit positive-coordinate condition uniquely fixes C=(R,R,R). Without it there would be eight sign choices.

parts.answer: Construct at a selected sphere point A the plane perpendicular to CA. The section area is pi*R^2*sin(phi)^2.
parts.reason: The cutting plane passes through A and makes angle phi with that tangent plane. Its center distance is h=R*cos(phi); the section radius satisfies r^2=R^2-h^2=R^2*sin(phi)^2. For the conventional nonobtuse plane angle, 0<=phi<=pi/2: the area is 0 at coincident tangent planes and pi*R^2 at a diametral section. A nondegenerate disk requires 0<phi<=pi/2. Area has length-squared units; h and r have length units.
A=(0,3,0) is on the radius-3 sphere; its tangent normal is A, giving 3y=9.
A=(0,2,-sqrt(5)) has norm squared 4+5=9. Its dot product with X must equal A.A=9; the negative z normal is essential.
A=(2,-2,-1) has norm squared 4+4+1=9. The tangent plane normal is A and its constant is 9, not the radius 3.

parts.answer: The tangent plane is mx+py+qz=R^2, assuming R>0 and m^2+p^2+q^2=R^2.
parts.reason: The plane through A normal to OA is m(x-m)+p(y-p)+q(z-q)=0. Since A lies on the sphere, this is mx+py+qz=R^2. Its normal has norm R, so its distance from the origin is R and its perpendicular foot is A. Theorem 37 proves tangency and uniqueness. Writing or selecting the equation alone is not a proof.
